findings.title: Allow team admins or owners rather than requiring both roles
findings.body: The permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, although either role should authorize managing a team booking. A team administrator who is neither the booking organizer nor an attendee will therefore receive FORBIDDEN. Use an OR check so administrators and owners can add guests to their team's bookings.

findings.title: Use the booking organizer's credentials for calendar updates
findings.body: This handler permits attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the logged-in user's identity and credentials. When someone other than the organizer invokes it, those credentials do not authorize updating the organizer's existing calendar event. The database attendee insertion has already completed, so this can leave Cal.com's guest list updated while the organizer's calendar remains unchanged, or fail the request after persisting the guests. Resolve the calendar credentials from the booking organizer instead.

findings.title: Deduplicate guests on the server before inserting attendees
findings.body: The uniqueGuests filter only excludes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within the submitted guests array. The server schema accepts duplicate addresses, so a direct request with the same new email twice passes validation and supplies two identical attendees to createMany. This can create duplicate attendee records and notifications, or fail the insertion if a database uniqueness constraint rejects them. Enforce uniqueness server-side rather than relying on the dialog's validation.

findings.title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is converted to lowercase, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. The email validator accepts uppercase characters, so submitting a case variant of a blacklisted address bypasses this restriction and causes an invitation to be sent to the blocked mailbox. Normalize incoming addresses for the blacklist comparison and existing-attendee checks.

findings.title: Honor event-type email suppression when sending guest updates
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee and does not accept event-type metadata. Other booking notification functions in this file honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding guests therefore sends standard notifications even for event types whose owners disabled them, potentially duplicating workflow emails. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the same suppression checks.

findings.title: Validate booking status before sending confirmed invitations
findings.body: The handler checks that the booking exists but never checks its status. An authorized caller can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking, after which the new email templates send calendar REQUEST attachments with status CONFIRMED and new guests receive scheduled-booking emails. Pending bookings can also reach this action through the existing past-pending edit menu. Reject unsupported booking statuses, or use status-appropriate notification behavior, rather than inviting people to events that are not confirmed.
